verdict.rationale: Both refactors keep behavior intact and split process_order into the same six readable steps with a shared _release helper. B is a little more faithful because it passes the actual `reserved` list into `_charge` instead of relying on reserved == order.items, as A does. B's characterization tests are broader: they cover the default tax rate, a used-up coupon, exact error messages, the INFO log line and non-PaymentDeclined gateway errors. B's report also flags a real latent bug, unreleased stock on unexpected gateway errors, and pins it with a test instead of changing it.
a_issues: `_charge` releases `order.items` instead of the reserved list. This is equivalent today but quietly depends on every item having been reserved.
`_tax` recomputes `_line_cents` separately from the subtotal sum, so line prices are computed twice.
Tests miss the default tax rate, a used-up coupon, non-PaymentDeclined gateway failures and the INFO paid log line.
b_issues: `_discount` and `_subtotal_and_tax` take whole Order/Customer objects instead of just the values they need, which couples them a bit more.
`_charge` has six parameters, threading `reserved` through just for the release.
One test comment is garbled ("rounding the sum (95) would give 95"), and the new test file duplicates `make_order` and `CUSTOMER` from test_checkout.py.

verdict.rationale: Both refactors keep behavior the same and produce a similar step-by-step `process_order`. A is a strictly mechanical move: it passes the actual `reserved` list into `_charge`. B swaps in `order.items`, which is equivalent today but couples `_charge` to the assumption that every item was reserved. A's characterization tests are stronger: they anchor exact error messages, check the log output, cover the unknown-country tax rate and used-up coupons, and pin the case where a non-`PaymentDeclined` gateway error is not released. A's report also accurately flags that last case as a likely real bug to fix separately.
a_issues: `_charge` takes six parameters, including `inventory` and `reserved`, only for cleanup on decline. This is slightly awkward, but it is the faithful translation.

One characterization test deliberately pins what is probably a bug (stock not released on an unexpected gateway error). That is correctly disclosed, but it will need to be updated when the bug is fixed.
b_issues: `_charge` releases `order.items` instead of the list of items actually reserved. This is behaviorally equivalent now, but it is a non-mechanical change in a refactor of production code and couples `_charge` to an assumption about the earlier step.
`_reserve_stock` no longer returns what it reserved, so the reserve and release relationship is implicit.
Parameter order is inconsistent across helpers, e.g. `_send_receipt(notifier, customer, order, ...)` versus the other helpers, which take `order` first.
`_tax` recomputes line totals separately from the subtotal; this is minor duplicated work.
Tests are weaker on exact messages (no anchors) and log assertions (substring on `caplog.text`), and they do not cover the unexpected gateway exception path, the default tax rate, or used-up coupons.
The report mentions an accidental CRLF conversion that was fixed. That is accurate but signals a fragile rewrite process.
